answer: Parallel lane vaulting: each identity gets a private juniper queue whose release order is fixed at admission. Agents must interleave calls across lanes; a burst pattern that only parallel identities can produce triggers a ferrous lockout, delaying all lanes for a full epoch. An attacker pays one epoch of latency per identity added, since each duplicate lane must independently wait through admission before its traffic counts. Cost scales linearly with fleet size, making mass identity cheapness worthless.
